description.narrative: (Uganda): The Inclusive Agricultural Markets Activity (IAM) works with agro-industry, the Government of Uganda (GOU), and private sector organizations to improve the agriculture market system. It works in the Global Food Security Strategy zones of influence, Karamoja, and the refugee-hosting districts.The Activity will use FY 2022 funds to: 1) improve access to high-quality agricultural products and services through strengthening input distribution networks and reducing counterfeit goods; 2) strengthen supply chains to help ensure effective movement of goods and services; 3) work with traders, exporters, millers, and processors to upgrade post-harvest handling, logistics, conditioning and storage, and manufacturing of commodities; 4) work with agro and food processors to improve the quality and nutritional value of food products; 5) build the capacity of small and medium food processors around food safety and quality standards, fortification and micro-nutrient enhancement, and food handling processes; and 6) support the seed systems market by engaging with farmer groups to produce high-quality declared seeds for nutrient dense beans and pulses.The Activity will also: 1) work with the GOU to improve the policy and regulatory framework for quality standards for agricultural products, managing counterfeits, and controlling aflatoxins in grains; 2) support service providers, including financial institutions, to supply affordable loans and insurance products; 3) strengthen the capacity of business development service providers to provide market and weather information and extension services; and 4) support farmer organizations and agribusinesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic to recover and become more resilient. The Activity will use funds to scale up interventions in Karamoja and refugee hosting districts (the resilience zone), and leverage private sector investments to build the capacity of agribusinesses and farmer organizations to engage in market activities...
